summary: Core authorization, bounded new-workflow payloads and immutable grading are covered by 33 emulator tests and browser acceptance. Production migration and legacy public/anonymous behavior require explicit review.

findings.issue: Legacy anonymous submissions preserve prior behavior and do not prove durable student identity; Canada Test 2 questions remain statically public.
findings.recommendation: Retain this explicit compatibility exception during rollout; use assigned durable identities and secure content collections for new protected assessments.

findings.issue: Rules intentionally accept bounded opaque response JSON; malformed direct writes can corrupt only the student-authored work for that attempt. They are detected before rendering and do not affect grading authority.
findings.recommendation: Keep revalidation and text-only rendering in every consumer; a future trusted validation backend may reject malformed JSON before storage.
